newsitem.title: MEXICO: SOCCER-NAPOLES SCORES FOUR AS GUADALAJARA WIN MEXICAN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NAPOLES SCORES FOUR AS GUADALAJARA WIN MEXICAN FINAL.

text.p: Gustavo Napoles scored four goals, all in the second half, as Guadalajara routed Toros Neza 6-1 to win the Mexican soccer championship on Sunday.
Guadalaraja, with a proud tradition of fielding only Mexican players in a championship awash with foreign stars, took the title for the 10th time in their history and the first in 10 years.
Guadalajara had drawn the first leg of the two-legged final 1-1 away and Neza managed to keep the score at 0-0 until halftime.
Napoles opened the floodgates with a 50th-minute strike, with Paulo Cesar Chavez adding a second almost immediately afterwards.
Napoles scored again in the 65th, 74th and 83rd minutes with Manuel Martinez completing the rout three minutes from the end. German Narangio scored Neza's consolation.

The only black mark for Guadalajara, who do not apply their Mexicans-rule to their coaches and are led by Brazilian Ricardo Ferreti, was that Mexican international Claudio Suarez was sent off in the 70th minute for elbowing an opponent.
It was Guadalajara's first red card of the championship.
The numbers were levelled, however, when Neza's Ramiro Romero was dismissed in an almost identical incident in the 82nd minute.
